Can you imagine a middle-class family being openly looted by a reputed and renowned corporate group like ICICI?? 
If you think it is safe to blindly trust employees of a well-known and well-regarded bank,  then you must watch this video to find out how this family's deposits worth Rs. 80-85 lakhs have been forfeited by the ICICI group. 
If you think that these clients signed the proposal forms for insurance policies and that therefore they only are to blame for the fiasco then you need to understand that an insurance company’s primary task is to underwrite the risk cover being sought by a prospective client. That is, the insurance company needs to satisfy itself if the prospective client is in a position to continue paying premiums regularly and if the risk cover being sought is as per the needs and requirements of the customer or not. This is done by way of verifying various declarations made in the insurance proposal form and the Agent Confidential report signed and submitted by the agent along with the proposal forms.

Also as per the Guidelines on Anti Money Laundering program for Insurers issued by IRDAI, the insurance company is mandated to ensure that the insurance being purchased by a customer is reasonable (i.e. as per the needs and requirements of the customer). Accordingly, the customer’s source of funds, his estimated net worth, etc., should be documented properly and the advisor and/or employee should obtain income proofs, to establish the customer’s need for insurance cover. Also, the requirement of exercising detailed due diligence for all customers paying premiums higher than 1 lakh per annum by the insurer is clearly and specifically mentioned in AML Guidelines.

The IRDA through its notifications has also mandated that all Life Insurance companies must adopt the practice of PIVC (Pre-Issuance Verification Call) to prevent mis-selling and unfair business practices and to ensure that during policy solicitation and sale stages, the prospects are fully informed and made aware of the terms and conditions of the product being sold. 

Hope the regulators put their foot down and ensure effective adherence to the laid down guidelines at least by reputed and renowned corporations like ICICI.

Groups like ICICI also have a moral and ethical responsibility towards their customers and they are bound by their code of conduct policies for zero tolerance to such frauds and employees involved in such acts deserve to be severely punished.

I’m extremely disappointed with the experience I’ve had with ICICI Prudential. Despite paying my premiums diligently for the past 6 years, the company is now asking for a long list of unnecessary and intrusive documents — including my last 3 years’ income proof, ITRs, personal documents, and even details of policies I hold with other companies.

This is highly frustrating and seems like a deliberate attempt to delay or increase the premium under the guise of formalities. I’m 100% healthy and fit — a fact confirmed by the medical test they themselves conducted.

Still, they are refusing to reinstate my policy even after submitting everything they asked for. This raises serious concerns about how difficult it might be if someone files a claim in the future.

This kind of poor service and lack of transparency is unacceptable from a company that claims to care for its customers. I would strongly advise others to reconsider before trusting ICICI Prudential with your insurance needs.

comments.text:
I'd like to share my bad experience with ICICI for the benefit of others.  I closed my bank account with ICICI after 18 years.  Unprofessional customer service.  

I started business with them in 2004 by opening an NRE and NRO account.  I was working abroad.  When I visited the branch once in 2010 or so, one of their managers tricked me into opening an ICICI Prudential Policy.  I had barely any balance in my account.  I told him that I didn't have any money to invest.  Just INR 50,000.  Maybe I'm gullible, but he convinced me somehow to invest INR 50,000.  I wasn't very bright with financial matters in those days. I tried to escape by saying I don't have my cheque book.  He sent his colleague home with me on a bike to collect the cheque.  I was actually in a hurry as I had to fly out of India the same day.  I gave him the cheque like a fool.  After I flew to my destination, I checked my bank balance in my NRO account and there were barely a few rupees left.  I can't remember what all I went through but I had problems because of the low balance.  I finally deposited cash into it.  

Then, I received reminders a year later to pay another amount.  After corresponding with them, I learnt that it was a recurring deposit policy.  For 5 years, I was supposed to pay 50,000.  The manager didn't tell me that.  I did not even receive the policy document.  I had to write to them several emails to finally get it.  

I was told during one of my visits that the money would grow upon maturity.  Each time I visited a branch, some employee would invite me to invest in an ICICI Prudential Policy.  I think, I ended buying 3 policies after I was convinced that I would receive a very good payout after maturity. 

I visited an ICICI branch in UAE once, where an employee quietly advised me to withdraw the policies because I was over 50 years of age.   She said your money will not grow.  In fact, you will lose your money.  I immediately applied to close the policies.  Right enough, the money that came in hand was lesser than the amount that I had deposited over the years.

Believe me, I made the right decision of closing my bank account.  I used to be proud initially of having an account with one of the best banks in India.  SRK and Amitabh were the brand ambassadors in advertisements.

I have made some Guaranteed Life insurance policies from  Bajaj Allianz agent who was working from the branch of one of these Well known private banks like ICICI. But she came to my house and explained the policy more or less. For the benefit of those who dont know. What i understood.
1) Guaranteed policies are those where we need to continue to pay the premiums yearly or as agreed by you. After all premiums are paid, you can withdraw but best to keep till maturity for best return. Often the amt recieved then is taxfree if we pay GST +premium amt.called 10(10D). Premium also gives 80 C benefit. 
Made market linked policy from Max. Not happy. 
2) But Market linked may be risky. Have to wait 5yrs and can withdraw. Not less. But can wait till maturity if doing well. Be in touch with bann and Agent. I stopped paying premium seeing value low. But will withdraw when 5yrs are completed.
Mutual fund; This has good liquidity. Lot of people choose this over Fixed Deposits as interest is much more. Best if you dont sell for one year.

This happened to me recently after Citi Bank migrated accounts to Axis Bank. My relationship manager arranged for a group call with an investment expert. They were trying to convince me that my FDs are not giving good returns, so insurance is better for me. So please be careful when the so called relationship managers talk to you, try to understand what their motives are, who those third part agents are.

Indian banks do not maintain confidentiality of you bank accounts. Your account details end up in the hands unscrupulous thirty parties. Recently i opened an account with ICICI. Clearly they were commission agents working with the bank. Banks don't care about the  customers, rather work with these agents because it is a win-win situation for them. comments.text: A relative is 70, and she went to her Union Bank branch for something to do with her account. The bank also sells life insurance under the SUD Life brand, and an agent approached her for life insurance. He said that if she died, her granddaughter would get the payout. He filled out the form, and the print was so small this 70-year-old relative couldn't read it. She signed the form, and a premium of 50,000 was deducted from her account. When the policy came, she found that she was the policy holder (the person paying the premium), her daughter was the life assured, and if the daughter died, the granddaughter would get the payout. She questioned the agent, and he said it was a clerical error and the correction was a mere formality. The 15-day cooling-off period was wasted like this. When she complained to the bank, they said, "You signed the form, and it's your fault." The insurance ombudsman kept asking for unnecessary proof over and over even after she provided them with everything. In the end she decided to forget the money and cancelled the policy. The truth is that the IRDAI doesn't allow life insurance sales to senior citizens. And agents routinely lie to senior citizens, get their money and then write policies on some relative's name.

I worked for sometime in call centre here in SMC (Pratap Nagar) in Delhi long back in 2012-13. There they use to sell ICICI policies to people not through companies channels but through their personal handsets(so there won't be any record of the conversation) and company was well aware of what was happening on the floor.

They ask for customer's data from there peers in different branches of those who already had policies and threaten them that their existing policy might collapse if they don't opt for the policy they are offering. They made deal sound like either the policy they are selling is supplimentary to their already existing policy and won't be heavy on pocket or their existing policy would lapse if they won't go for the policy they are being offered.

Every Team of 10-12 people had such great 2-3 storyteller acting as seniors who were assigned to lock such deals. In those days I had personally seen them selling 5-6 policies, one over another, to a single person, preying on their fear and lack of knowledge, which the person couldn't pay and ultimately all getting lapsed, but atleast they achieved their targets.

Although I left company in 3rd month but I believe it still continues today. Never ever go for their words. Agents put a lot of personal touch well over and above than what's true to lure customers. Always be careful and always ask for everything in writing so atleast later you'll have a say!

comments.text: I was working in the banking sector in a similar third party relationship with an insurance company. M not taking the side of the bank or the insurance company here. All i want to say is that I feel, what leads the employees of banks and insurance companies to such mis selling is the extreme work pressures through irrational targets set by their managers and directors. The reality on the ground is quite different. It is probably a middle class citizen working at these banks with mega financial dreams (nothing wrong with having high aspirations) trying desperately to make it large in life without realising that it takes a lot of hard/smart work and patience to get there. They see such opportunities as shortcuts to get them closer to their dreams. This segment of society is also the most competitive and cut throat that they are willing to do anything to get to their goals. Morals are secondary at this point.  Thank you for sharing ur experience. I hope it helps you recover ur funds at the earliest. Keep up the good work Insurance Angels.

comments.text:
Same thing happened with me in early 2020. My father had just retired & wanted to do an FD from ICICI Bank. Very smartly, the ICICI Bank Executive mis-selled a ICICI PRULIFE Policy in the name of a "Scheme". But, upon receipt of Hard & Soft Copies of the Policy, I immediately saw that something was wrong. As the policy was in the Free Look Period, I immediately cancelled it online as well through the Bank Manager. I must commend the Bank Manager, he scolded the Executive in front of us, cancelled the Policy and made sure we got back our Funds within 7 days. Also, the Executive got transferred and we got our Funds back with Interest. However, to my surprise, the Manager was also transferred within the next month. So, its not that everyone is bad @ ICICI Bank. Present Manager & Deputy Manager at my Branch are very co-operative and since then, I have not heard any mis-selling @ my branch.

My personal advise to investors: Invest only in an FD from ICICI Bank & nothing else, because everything else is sandwiched with some scrupulous scheme. Also, take the FD NOTE within 7-10 days of issuance. Even if any Scheme / Policy is issued, it will have 30 days Free Look Period, within this time if cancelled all funds can be retrieved easily.

SBI is also in the pool.

They were able to pay for few years with their savings but later realized that if they stop paying premium without completing the premium payment term than a big chunk of their premium already paid will be forfeited. 
Also just to let you know that the insurer is made responsible to verify the annual income of all the client's especially of those clients who are proposing insurance policies with more than 1 lakh premium in a year. The regulations are clear that the insurer must sell the policies only after understanding the needs and requirements of the client and basis their premium paying capacity. 
I hope you understand my point.
Many thanks

@InsuranceAngels  100% agreed to your point. It is almost criminal what they did. I am sure these 2-3 people must have made this scheme together to get their targets and make some commissions on the side.  I don't know if there are any ways to file cases and get justice served against specific employees involved. I hope that happens. 

But as a customer we should also be careful about our investment. Relationship Managers are not money managers allocated to make profits for us. Their job is to make processes easy in case if we want to do any investments. We shouldn't put our blind faith and money with them.

Looking at how many policy documents this family had in their hands I am wondering if they really checked how these FDs or FDesque investments worked and where they could verify their investments. It's not matter of a few hundreds afterall.  ICICI bank has one of the best phone apps. It takes just a couple touches to check all your investments with Bank.  If they did that they would have immediately noticed their money is not with bank (as ICICI Pru investments won't show up in bank app).

When it comes to investing money, one should be very aware and alert about it.  Otherwise we end up in situations like this unfortunate family is in.  It is very frustrating process to get that money back.  I hope and wish they get all their money.

comments.text: My wife and I had a similar experience at ICICI Bank in  2019. We had settled in US in 2016 with our first daughter. Our second daughter is in Canada. In 2019 February we sold our independent house in Coimbatore and invested the proceeds in ICICI Bank, Indian Bank, Indian Overseas Bank. We already had old savings account in these banks. We came to the ICICI branch and met the manager, a lady, who is currently no longer in service. We gave application to invest INR 30 lakhs. The lady manager issued us FDRs for 27 lakhs and told us that we take insurance policy in our daughter’s name for 30L for which the 3L was utilized as first payment. In 2020 February the bank foreclosed our two FDs for 5L without our consent and utilized that to pay premium of 5 L for the insurance policy. We had come to India that time and met the manager and questioned how dare they did that. She spoke very sweetly and said we will get a higher return than FDs. We visited the branch next morning taking my B in law, who was a leading ICWA and had contacts with many top people. He told bluntly that he will sue the ICICI and it’s better to reverse the actions immediately. The bank manager agreed and restored our foreclosed FDs. In the meanwhile Rs 7 L had already been paid to their insurance wing. Our FDs were all AUTO RENEWAL type.The manager said that the insurance policy will be kept in LAPSE and after five years we will get back the money with nominal interest. The matter stands there.We never responded to repeated requests to pay premium. In 2022 we visited the bank and found that the lady manager had left the service.our daughter in Canada was the policy holder.She had never come to that bank and was a Canadian citizen. Our daughter had never signed anywhere to get the policy. Someone in the bank had signed in her place. The bank officers clearly played mischief knowing that we live far far away and our visits to India will be for a limited period only. This video further explains the nefarious actions of that bank.

comments.text: I represented a 40 railway employees against SBILife Insurance who were sold the life Insurance policies in the pretext of FD investment scheme. They were promised that it was just a single premium policy and then the agent got the signature for a 5 year term policy. The premium amount was kept as high as 3 lakhs and for some of them it was more than their annual income.  They were promised that they would be paying this only once. Now as per the policy terms, if you don't pay the second premium the policy lapses and the money goes to the insurance company which is a direct profit for them. They kept the premium at high amount because they knew that the clients won't be able to pay the high premium the next time. With different arm twisting exercise which included criminal proceedings and consumer case against them I was able to get the money back for the clients and get the full time SBI employee sacked. This is a very crazy world. My humble request is not to sign on any piece of paper without fully going through the papers and don't trust blindly anyone who's selling you any financial product.

comments.text:
Sorry for this family, but honestly, the real problem here is financial illiteracy of a majority of people.

A quick read of documents will easily tell you that it's a policy. Moreover, there are no savings products in ICICI with the name "Prudential". They are all policies. The fact that they have several policy documents clearly mentioning ICICI Prudential and never realized what they were is sad.

There's definitely foul-play from bank and agents IF they passed these off as RD or FD, but this is a bit like signing on a blank paper for this family. You cannot trust what the other party is gonna write on that paper afterwards. There are problems on both sides here.

A few tips to prevent this happening to you:
1. NEVER sign something without reading it. Doesn't matter how lucrative something is, or how trusted the other party is. It's your money, and ultimately your responsibility where you put it. RBI has rules to prevent foul-play, but your safety and financial security is first and foremost your own responsibility.
2. If you don't feel qualified enough to understand all the policy documents, take help from a reputed CA. They will likely charge you some amount, but it'll make everything MUCH safer for you going forward.
3. If something mentions "High returns" or "Tax free", that's a reason to be more vigilant, not less. Policies like these do give higher returns (potentially), but also carry higher risks. There's no such thing as high-return. It's always high-return-high-risk. Assess your own risk profile. If you're in your 20s and making a lot of money, you can afford take more risks. If you're near retirement, avoid high risk investments like plague.
5. Spend a little time educating yourself on finance. It doesn't matter what your background is. Finance is necessary education for all of us and it's sad it's not a part of curriculum in schools and colleges.

comments.text:
My father got retired in 2017 as a Professor of English  (Govt. of HP). An insurance agent from PNB Metlife visited him within a couple of days, and told about a plan to invest the funds received during retirement. The plan, as per him, was "give 1.5 lacs per year for 3 years, and get 10 lacs after 10 years". He was handed over a cheque of the said amount. And that's when, my father had signed an endowment plan that actually required 5 instalments of 1.5 lacs each for 5 years. We got suspicious when a fourth instalment was deducted when the bank balance reached the premium amount. (My dad had used his FD for some emergency). We tried to surrender the policy, but we were told something which should have been told in the first place (i.e We will charge 50-60% tax if you surrender this 10 year policy).   Long sotry short, our mistake was that we trusted that agent and didn't even care about reading the policy document (esp. the table given at the end of most policies). And to add to our wounds, another such policy of Rs 1 lac p.a was sold to us in 2018 under the impression that it was aN RD. 

If there's any way to get our money back, kindly let me know. 

Anyways, it is a very informative video. The way you have communicated with complainants, speaks volumes of the expertise you hold. Well done!

comments.text:
Greetings!! Anjani Ma'am,
This family is required to invest 25 lakhs every year for next 7-8 years to earn the returns on their invested 80 lakh rupees. If they fail to deposit the amount of 25 lakhs every year then as per the provisions of the policies that have been sold to them they will have to bear huge losses and might even end up losing the entire invested amount. 
It is true that they should have read the documents on receipt and such a situation could have ben avoided. However, I must humbly submit that as per norms even the insurance company was required to verify if the client was actually in a position to deposit the premiums every year or not. It was insurance company's responsibility to have conducted a detailed due diligence on client before issuing such toxic policies with such high premium payment obligations. IRDAI norms put a complete responsibility upon the insurance company. 
There should have been verification calls made by insurance company's call centre employees prior to issuance of these policies but no such calls were made either. 
Therefore to put the entire responsibility on the client and to give a complete clean chit to the insurance company would not be correct. Many Regards

Greetings!! Kunal Kotiwal Sir,
Multiple insurance policies have been sold to this family under the garb of issuing (hybrid) fixed deposits without following the norms and regulations of the regulating authorities and now the amount deposited by this family in these multiple insurance policies is under danger of getting forfeited by the insurance company because this family is not in a position to continue premium payment in these policies.12 out 14 policies sold to this family are traditional plans which have very strict premium forfeiture clauses. Greetings!! Sir,
I agree with the majority of your points and am grateful to have such a knowledgeable audience on my channel. In conclusion, I'd like to respectfully suggest that society is built on trust values, and we can't expect everybody to know everything. A doctor should have faith in an engineer, and vice versa. These people put their trust in their bankers and advisors, but they were duped. It's not correct to say that this is totally their fault. I hope you would appreciate my concerns. 

Multiple insurance policies have been sold to this family under the garb of issuing (hybrid) fixed deposits without following the norms and regulations of the regulating authorities and now the amount deposited by this family in these multiple insurance policies is under danger of getting forfeited by the insurance company because this family is not in a position to continue premium payment in these policies.12 out 14 policies sold to this family are traditional plans which have very strict premium forfeiture clauses. Only 2 plans are ULIP, wherein these people will have their amount refunded after completion of 5 policy years. All these years they were aware that the amount is getting deducted but they were not aware that it is being deducted towards a product which has extremely harsh premium forfeiture clause. 
The insurance company was required to verify if or not the client can make regular premium payment in policy and because the insurance company did not performed it's task properly the family is getting punished and the insurance company is being benefitted although the entire fault is of the insurance company only.

comments.text:
ULIP is the worst thing you can do with your money. Never ever mix insurance and investment. Go for term insurance which is about 4-5 times of your annual income + your other liabilities like loans. Then invest in market - if you dont have anough time or knowledge to research on individual company, take Mutual Fund route and stay invested for long term (5 years+), use SIP option to average out in case market goes down. If there is a loss in short term, dont panic sell. Stay invested for many many years. If you dont have knowkedge, never try to time the market. And Finally, STAY AWAY FROM ULIPS.

So, to summarize - 
1. Iterm Insurance - about 5 times of your annual income + Liability
2. Health Insurance - minimum 10L floater for you and the family
3. Long term investment in good stocks with mix of small and mid cap with Nifty 50, if no knowledge, go for Mutual Funds
4. NO ULIPS at ANY COST

This is not the problem of only ICICI Bank. You will find these  leaches at every private bank.

comments.text:
Greetings!! Sir,
Multiple insurance policies have been sold to this family under the garb of issuing (hybrid) fixed deposits without following the norms and regulations of the regulating authorities and now the amount deposited by this family in these multiple insurance policies is under danger of getting forfeited by the insurance company because this family is not in a position to continue premium payment in these policies.12 out 14 policies sold to this family are traditional plans which have very strict premium forfeiture clauses. Only 2 plans are ULIP, wherein these people will have their amount refunded after completion of 5 policy years. The insurance company was required to verify if or not the client can make regular premium payment in policy and because the insurance company did not performed it's task properly the family is getting punished and the insurance company is being benefitted although the entire fault is of the insurance company only.

comments.text:
I had a similar experience with ICICI, I had a bank account with ICICI from 2002 around 2005 I decided to close it since I was not using it not maintaining any balance so I gave the requested to close my account. Submitted all the documents even after that I was getting email from ICICI for my monthly Bank statement. Where they showing that I had to pay the Bank for not maintaining the minimum balance. I forwarded the email from ICICI along with scanned copy of closure to almost all the customer support email that I could find on ICICI website also copied, my branch manager, regional manager, and district head. After sending this email I got a call in 2 hours from my bank manager begging me to hold the account for free. Taking the picture of closing request saved me.

Not only ICICI, HDFC life has such scams as well. I stopped investing in IRDA policies. 
If any one ask you to invest just ask them to explain the math. only 50%-60% of what you pay will be mentioned as sum assured. The rest of it will be part of bonus, This depends on market and how well the entity performed. 

The only best one that I feel safe is LIC Term plan or Life Insurance - Do not rely on any agent gather the info on LIC website or via LIC offices.

If you are holding any Credit Cards make sure you have cap on daily spending limit. 
If you are closing your card, make sure to keep a copy of written or e-mail request, also ask the provider confirmation of closing via email(official email) or letter. If not call them and inform them you are recording the conversation and get the confirmation of closure of your Credit Card. 

If you are having any bank account, even ICICI or HDFC. or HSBC ask for a passbook under current rules Bank should provide one.

comments.text: Whats happened with this family is very tragic. To have lost ones entire savings, its unthinkable. In money matters, one can't trust the RM or any bank official blindly. One needs to read all documents, compare with products across banks /institutions before taking the decision. It's not that banks encourage employees to dupe customers. In today's world where even a small mistake / cheating gets amplified in social media, a Bank cannot afford to have the slightest dent on its reputation. These are a few isolated instances of fraud by some officials. The only thing that can protect an investor from such an incident is awareness and vigilance. One should try and understand everything about the agreement / investment that one's signing up for. If you don't know how the product will make money for you, then don't get into that product. Stick to plain FD, RD or MFs.  Most important is that people need to be 100 times careful if a product sounds too good to be true - for example 15 percent consistent returns per year in future without any risk. If someone tells me about such a product, then i will walk out of the meeting the very next moment. Products may have generated 30% returns per annum but past performance does not guarantee future returns. There is always higher risk in such products. If a product having 15% risk-free return exists, then banks will not get any depositors, all of us will rather put our money in such products.

It is difficult to watch that mother in this video, she would have served the executive of this bank with humility and honesty during her service years only to be cheated by them and rob her of her hard earned money. It is a shame that there is no oversight on such practices of banks, it seems in India private banks have their way around the system and no one cares while people suffer.

Important things to remember however, are:
1) Banks are for current, savings account and to make FD or RD. nothing else!
2) Never agree to anything over phone
3) Never take unsolicited calls from any bank personnel
4) If someone calls from bank and tries to market any product, ask to meet them in person at the branch you frequently visit
5) Ask written documents about everything that is promised and understand everything in only 4 terms described in point 1 above!
6) Do not keep more than Rs 5 lacs in bank account and better trust SBI over icici thugs.

Multiple insurance policies have been sold to this family under the garb of issuing (hybrid) fixed deposits without following the norms and regulations of the regulating authorities and now the amount deposited by this family in these multiple insurance policies is under danger of getting forfeited by the insurance company because this family is not in a position to continue premium payment in these policies.12 out 14 policies sold to this family are traditional plans which have very strict premium forfeiture clauses. Only 2 plans are ULIP, wherein these people will have their amount refunded after completion of 5 policy years. The insurance company was required to verify if or not the client can make regular premium payment in policy and because the insurance company did not performed it's task properly the family is getting punished and the insurance company is being benefitted although the entire fault is of the insurance company only.

When a bank employee says you will get 15% returns on your deposits, you also need to think how is it that other banks are paying 7 to 8 % maximum on fixed deposits, while this bank is paying 15% on deposits?  These are obviously educated people and should have checked the deposit receipts and documents clearly to see if they show these high fixed returns.  My advise to people is not to be blinded with promise of high returns and to get proper receipts and documents showing the promised returns in writing. Otherwise don't go ahead with the deposit. Multiple insurance policies have been sold to this family under the garb of issuing (hybrid) fixed deposits without following the norms and regulations of the regulating authorities and now the amount deposited by this family in these multiple insurance policies is under danger of getting forfeited by the insurance company because this family is not in a position to continue premium payment in these policies.12 out 14 policies sold to this family are traditional plans (namely Icici Pru Future Perfect, Icici Pru Guaranteed Savings Insurance Plan, Icici Pru Assured Savings Insurance Plan and Icici Pru Cash Back) which have very strict premium forfeiture clauses. Years before I purchased HDFC ULIP - Investment cum insurance plan with some medical benefits. I was told by agent that I need to pay only for 5 years and the policy warrants the coverage for 25 years. To my surprise I started getting notice to continue paying the premiums for next 20 years. If I don't pay then my credits will be utilized from the total and be spent on fund management, policy management etc. I paid 90000 for  5 years, I opted to withdraw my money and ended up in loss of 18000. Luckily I got 72000 back. Since then I only approach direct employees of Govt Recognized Insurance companies for any type of investments like medihealth, vehicle insurance, etc. Even for home loan I opted for LIC HFL. 

I suggest do not go with private banks for any type of services except banking.

comments.text:
Mr. Nitin Balchandaniji, I would like to thank you wholeheartedly for bringing up this fact to the common people. I can understand the amount of the pain this family have been going through. I'm pretty sure this bank played dirty tricks to others too. ICICI/HDFC/Bharat AXA approached many a times to buy their policies though I didn't buy. 
Sir, there are few suggestions; 
1) Policy purchasing document must be translated in regional languages. 2) This language must be understandable and easy to read. 
3) Letters must  be in normal size (not in ultra small size which is very difficult to read. 
4) Conversations between the customer and the sales representative must be video recorded to have the clarity between promised versus actual. Subsequently the video recording must be shared with the customer and must be restored at their side too. 
6) As Mutual Fund, few Life Insurance policies are  subject to the market risks so they must promise logical, minimum return and clarify the amount of risk associated with it (which means the amount you are going to loose at dull times). If these companies have the ability to predict the return in good times then why not at dull times. 
7) Common people literally don't know where to go,  how to complain, to lodge complaint against whom. 
8) We should come up with a plan with the help of legal experts to find out the loopholes in their guidelines/the whole process (from saling a policy to the maturity) so that we can make both the agent and the company accountable.
9) We should write a letter to the Govt. that the govt.should issue a mandate to these banks/companies  to create awareness among customers at both rural and urban areas by utilizing their CSR fund. 
10) Does anyone remember when you have last participated or have been invited either by the Govt. or Private to any investment awareness camp to be an informed customer. We should request the Govt. of India to consider this request. 
I'm a doctor by profession. I'm not an expert in this field. I shared my views what I feel. I'll always be there to support you as per my capacity. Sorry for the lengthy writing. Thanks again.

comments.text: Every private retail bank in India has become a slaughterhouse. Every bank has a tie up with insurance companies e.g. HDFC Bank has a tie up with HDFC Life, ICICI Bank has tie up with ICICI Prudential. In every bank, there is a desk allocated for insurance staff, so HDFC Life staff will be sitting in the HDFC bank. In addition, all bank staffs are giving targets to sell insurance products. Be that the welcome desk or Relationship Manager ever staff has targets.  Every morning and evening there is a huddle & Branch Manager will shout and ask how many policies have been sold. Staff to protect their jobs and to save themselves from daily humiliation are left with no choice but to sell, usually customers don't want to buy insurance products, so staff are forced to missell the insurance products as FD or RD with 15 - 20% return. It's all bull shit. These products are linked to market so performance of the insurance policies depend on the market performance. They will have all fancy names for these products. The staff who achieves his target gets promotion, the Relationship Manager gets promotion and incentives. Coz the Branch has achieved its target the Branch Manager gets a promotion. The insurance agent gets his commission plus if he has achieved his target a foreign trip.  Staff who are unable to sell or who refuses to sell coz they don't find it ethical are given very less rating, so say a cashier has not met his insurance sales target but has worked hard 365 days, caught fraudulent notes, handled the long queues of customers, never had shortage of cash, came everyday during covid risking his life will be given an appraisal as poor performance which in turn affects his bonus and he never gets a promotion. Everyone in banking is aware of misselling, from the security guard to the top management. HDFC Bank is the worst bank, go and speak to any HDFC Bank employee. The way they are pressurized to sell insurance policies. If they can't sell, the Branch Manager sends them to Cluster Head (CH) office where the CH insults and threatens them "if u can't sell insurance, look for a job somewhere else". Then the Zonal Head (ZH) will come in picture, he again threatens the staff.  RBI needs to intervene here and ask banks to stop selling insurance products. If a customer wants insurance policy he can visit an Insurance office.  Because of this misselling, most sensible customers have stopped visiting branches and prefer online banking. But then even they are not saved, coz the Relationship Manager  lands on his door, Sir, ek bohut acha investment plan aya hai, 20% guaranteed return hai, sign these papers and the cycle continues. Another bakra halal.

These people are not actors. This is a true story, and the people in the video have actually lost the money mentioned in the video. In reality, every case discussed on this channel is true. 
I'd like to share the reply filed in Rajya Sabha by Hon'ble Minister of State for Finance Shri Anuraag Singh Thakur to the questionnaire sent by us through Hon'ble MP Shri Binoy Viswam:  https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X8ZHL3WkKjrJL31MBUVSypbjd2STNaw9/view?usp=drivesdk  
We have filed all the 316 cases which have been referred to in the reply, and 254 of them resulted in mis-sold policies being cancelled and the money being refunded to them. As a result, we can proudly say to have a resolution rate of more than 92 percent. Multiple insurance policies have been sold to this family under the garb of issuing (hybrid) fixed deposits without following the norms and regulations of the regulating authorities and now the amount deposited by this family in these multiple insurance policies is under danger of getting forfeited by the insurance company because this family is not in a position to continue premium payment in these policies.12 out 14 policies sold to this family are traditional plans which have very strict premium forfeiture clauses. comments.text: I am an ex employee of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance. Level 4 Manager that's a mid level managerial position. ICICI Bank is the Banca Channel of ICICI Prudential.  Bank generate "Fee Income" when they sell insurance products. Fee Income from insurance products are higher than FDs. So they generally target FD customers and cross sell them insurance products in the name of recurring deposits, "Neha Poddar" is probably an ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Employee in whose code the insurance policy is logged in. They most probably forge signatures and get the PAN & Aadhaar Data from Bank database, kindly get a forensic done on the signature it's admissable in the court of law. The last page of the policy bond contains the signed copy of the insurance application form.They enter an incorrect mobile number or a mobile number of known person (friend). So the verification call do happen where they themselves verify. On branch it broke my heart to see a senior citizen losing his money kept for his daughter marriage in traditional insurance product. I got promoted to Branch Head but I resigned still. I lost my  yearly bonus of 1.5lakhs but I don't regret it. I dont have blood money. But the working environment is toxic. Currently I am working for IDBI Bank, where we are not that tech savy but I see LIC products sold on a better way. One advise I always give is that if you are not informed about the policy apply for a freelook with 15-30 days. If you write a strong worded mail -I have seen freelook happening for even 1 year policy, but after 1 year only legal system can help. Remember always current FD rates are 5-6%, Recurring Deposits rates are lower than FDs generally and in case of traditional insurance products all premium need to be paid otherwise it's forfeited. In case of ULIP if you disconnect the ECS you can get back the principal amount after 5 years(lockin period). In case of any query/help/insider information. Do contact.

Going by your words which says that the value has been going up and down it must be a ULIP. See insurance advisor of ICICI Pru Life sell policies in the name of very high returns (double digits) by showing historical returns of the funds. But in actuality it's never the case, there are a loads of charges associated with ULIPs like Premium allocation charge, Fund Management Charge, Mortality Charge(If your age is high it's also high), monthly premium have an added charge, GST@18% on premiums gets deducted before investment. You will find detailed breakup about these charges on the policy bond. In actuality because of these charges the returns comes around single digit if the fund performs good/ negative return if the fund perform bad. My Advice you should keep the ULIP because it provides you with Life Insurance that is around 20 times of the annual premium that is around 600,000.  which will be payable in case of death. In case you don't want a life insurance or you have a full fledged life insurance policy then sell this policy. Now when you will visit nearest ICICI Prudential office to sell this policy (don't visit ICICI Bank) they might recommend you "switching" your policy to a high profitable policy but you ignore them and tell them that you need your money back strictly. And always check where you are signing. If you don't receive your money within 14-21 days issue formal complaint and dont hesitate to reach out for legal help.

This is someting which happens all over India. Expecially in rural area where ICICI Bank has its branches. Its all because of Employe fedility. To be very accurate when you are taking such product. 


1. Always ask sales person to fill the proposal form in front of you. Once filled. Review it. 
2. Take a copy of Proposal Form. Try to take the acknowledgement also. 
3. Always ask sales person to share his employee ID and also official Email ID. 
4. Please ask for all the features to be communicated over the email before you signup. 


If you tell these things. Person will not do. I have been saved too many times by using these tricks. 


Cheers.

comments.text:
Greetings!! Priyanka Godse Ma'am,
Multiple insurance policies have been sold to this family under the garb of issuing (hybrid) fixed deposits without following the norms and regulations of the regulating authorities and now the amount deposited by this family in these multiple insurance policies is under danger of getting forfeited by the insurance company because this family is not in a position to continue premium payment in these policies.12 out 14 policies sold to this family are traditional plans which have very strict premium forfeiture clauses. Only 2 plans are ULIP, wherein these people will have their amount refunded after completion of 5 policy years. The insurance company was required to verify if or not the client can make regular premium payment in policy and because the insurance company did not performed it's task properly the family is getting punished and the insurance company is being benefitted although the entire fault is of the insurance company only.

comments.text:
Greetings!! Hemu G Sir,
I'm afraid I'm going to have to disagree with you. Our society is built on the foundation of trust. We can't expect everyone to be well-versed in everything. This family put their trust in their bankers and advisors, but they were deceived. We're also not claiming that this is exclusive to Icici Bank. However, I have no qualms in stating that Icici bank staff have committed the most egregious and vicious examples of mis-selling that I have seen. Let me share a few examples with you, and you can decide for yourself whether any reputable company would treat its customers in this manner. I should also say that when these situations were reported on our platform, the firm launched an internal inquiry, and after conducting their own inquiry, they decided to cancel the mis-sold plans and return the premiums paid by these clients:
1. https://youtu.be/eF3CjQpI4nM
2. https://youtu.be/ip6axA3WI_w
3. https://youtu.be/4PnXCheX7uw
comments.author: @InsuranceAngels

comments.text:
I'd also like to share the reply filed in Rajya Sabha by Hon'ble Minister of State for Finance Shri Anuraag Singh Thakur to the questionnaire sent by us through Hon'ble MP Shri Binoy Viswam:  https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X8ZHL3WkKjrJL31MBUVSypbjd2STNaw9/view?usp=drivesdk  
We have filed all the 316 cases which have been referred to in the reply, and 254 of them resulted in mis-sold policies being cancelled and the money being refunded to them. Mis-sold products were cancelled in 39 other cases, and new plans with a single pay premium were issued as per customer needs. Just 23 cases have been turned down. As a result, we can proudly say to have a resolution rate of more than 92 percent. Also, please watch our recent video about a 3.5 crore scam perpetrated by HDFC life and RBL bank employees on a senior citizen; we assisted him in having his money refunded, and this client's daughter can be seen praising our work at the end of the video:
https://youtu.be/d2ErOFnuYwE
If even one video on this channel had been malevolent or an attempt at mudslinging, I would have been hit with defamation cases that my seven generations would have been unable to pay. I hope you can see where I'm coming from. Fighting for a cause takes bravery, and no one has said that all of Icici's staff or products are awful. It's just that a few bad apples have tarnished the institution as a whole. Icici's senior management has failed terribly in nailing such elements.

comments.text:
This is something i commonly face whenever i try to withdraw money , or whenever i visit a bank. Relationship managers start connecting you with insurance providers outside the bank. 

The talk will mostly go around section 10 10 (D) , and guaranteed 12% and this product also gives you insurance as well blah blah. Life is a bed of roses etc. 
I always push them for official documentation and they give all sorts of excuses for not giving that . And sometimes you get a self generated pdf file as the official document. 

Rule of thumb is for any product go to the official website and read terms and conditions and then you get the real picture. Eventually when i work out return for these schemes i found that these schemes based on current NAV do a worse job than PPF or SSJ . 

Watch out for lock in period and penalties if you exit before the period ,  these stuff the marketing gentleman is never gonna talk to you about.
  The 12% guarantee will always be based on an NAV assumption the marketing gentleman has made and not based on actuals. In some cases i have seen actual returns even at 4-5% (this is almost a SB account interest rate)

Sad to hear about what happened to this family , but always one needs to remember the childhood moral we have learnt . Never put all your eggs in one basket.

Greetings!! Dear Prashanth Sir,
Multiple insurance policies have been sold to this family under the garb of issuing (hybrid) fixed deposits without following the norms and regulations of the regulating authorities. 12 out 14 policies sold to this family are traditional plans which have very strict premium forfeiture clauses. Their money is under the risk of getting forfeited by the insurance company. Only 2 plans are ULIP, wherein these people will have their amount refunded after completion of 5 policy years. The amount deposited by this family in these multiple insurance policies is under danger of getting forfeited by the insurance company because this family is not in a position to continue premium payment in these policies. The insurance company was required to verify if or not the client can make regular premium payment in policy and because the insurance company did not performed it's task properly the family is getting punished and the insurance company is being benefitted although the entire fault is of the insurance company only

comments.text:
It's too sad to see this. I hope this family gets their money back and also gets compensation from the Bank. I too have an account in ICICI bank. But I use it only for online transaction purposes, so I don't keep much money in it. There was a bad incident that happened with me in this bank after which I decided that I won't open any new main account in this bank. One day I was trying to pay my bill online and was waiting for OTP. I tried several times but OTP was not received. I thought maybe the telecom operator is facing congestion. I tried the next day and still, no OTP was received. I was not able to pay my bill on time. This started concerning me, that what could be the issue. Since I have internet banking, I decided to look at my profile. There I found that the registered mobile number was not the one I provided. Instead, there was some international number. I don't remember the country now, but this shocked me. I immediately called the bank and informed them about the issue. To which they reply that they don't change mobile numbers without doing KYC and they don't put the international mobile number as a registered number without getting passport details. I told them that I never did any KYC to change my number, nor I have ever traveled internationally. In fact, I never had a passport when I opened the account and I had never submitted my passport details to the bank. I asked them how this happened and why this happened. They replied nothing. They were just saying that they don't do it without KYC. I wish I should have done a police complaint against them at that time. But as I was afraid of losing my money since my registered number was different and that number had my OTP. I went to the bank, did all KYC again, changed my mobile number. Since then, I never keep any big amount in ICICI and neither I suggest this bank to anyone.
I do get a lot of calls from the bank to take RD or this policy that policy ... 0 EMI this 0 EMI that... I tell them that I have no source of income. Then they tell some schemes where I don't have to pay anything else other than a small annual premium etc etc... Then I have to make them understand that at least I will have to pay that small premium which I can't because I don't have income. My approach to handling them is that no matter how shiny their schemes look, never entertain their schemes.

comments.text:
First of all my deepest condolences to the family for their devastating financial loss and emotional distress. Thank you Mr. Nitin Balchandani for posting this awareness video! I would like to share my experience from an Insurance Agent perspective!

I got employed in a private bank as a "Life Advisor" (their fancy name for Insurance Agents). Initially, things were interesting but later on, our managers started to put pressure on many subordinates like me to sell policies that were not going to be that much beneficial for consumers. They had the wrong attitude of pressuring/luring the "Life Advisors" on the basis of getting attractive commissions to sell unfair policies to their customers!

Despite their pressure, I filtered only better policies that will be beneficial for the consumers and advised them to invest only if they fully understand and are genuinely interested in them. But after a certain point, I was not able to bring in any business to the company like other Life Advisors did because they sold their soul to the demon in the name of getting better commissions!

So I quit because I didn't want to earn lucrative commissions at the cost of my potential consumer's life savings! Please remember these things:

- Each consumer is different. You cannot sell the same policy for all the consumers just because you're getting better commissions.
- As an insurance agent one needs to understand their potential consumer's financial background, what their financial goals are and, which insurance policy from your company will be most beneficial for their prospective consumer.
- Work towards fulfilling the goals of the consumer rather than becoming heartless slaves of lucrative commissions.
- As a consumer, kindly scrutinize the juicy facts of earning lucrative returns pitched to you. Simply see if you can afford the product and then see if the pitched product will meet your financial goals. If not just say "NO".

Wish everyone good health and wealth!

Thank you! 🙏

comments.text:
Greetings!! Paresh Joshi Sir,
I'm afraid I'm going to have to disagree with you. Our society is built on the foundation of trust. We can't expect everyone to be well-versed in everything. This family put their trust in their bankers and advisors, but they were deceived. We're also not claiming that this is exclusive to Icici Bank. However, I have no qualms in stating that Icici bank staff have committed the most egregious and vicious examples of mis-selling that I have seen. Let me share a few examples with you, and you can decide for yourself whether any reputable company would treat its customers in this manner. I should also say that when these situations were reported on our platform, the firm launched an internal inquiry, and after conducting their own inquiry, they decided to cancel the mis-sold plans and return the premiums paid by these clients:
1. https://youtu.be/eF3CjQpI4nM
2. https://youtu.be/Qjyb0jYyouo
3. https://youtu.be/4PnXCheX7uw
We have received 316 complaints against Icici as of March 23, 2021, with 254 of those complaints resulting in the cancellation of mis-sold products and the processing of refunds. Only 23 complaints were denied, and 39 mis-sold products were cancelled and replaced with new policies with a single premium payment. This indicates that in over 92 percent of cases when customers sought the company directly and were denied any form of assistance, their concerns were resolved once they were published to our channel. What conclusions may we draw as a result of this? Here is the document for your reference: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X8ZHL3WkKjrJL31MBUVSypbjd2STNaw9/view?usp=drivesdk
On a questionnaire submitted by us through Hon'ble M.P. Shri Binoy Viswam, this was filed in Rajya Sabha by Hon'ble Minister of State for Finance, Mr. Anuraag Singh Thakur.

comments.text:
I have been through this but fortunately  my stake wasn't so big. Got frauded by an Insurance Company that tied up with a private bank where I had an account. I was also told it's like an FD with life coverage! They targetted all senior citizens, giving them the "temptation" of better interest than FDs! Most people fell for it, especially because of the life coverage! Plus I was told to pay a premium for 3 years only, then not touch the amount for 5 years after which I could withdraw. I got to know when in the 5th year I got a letter saying I haven't paid for 2 years! And the bank associating with this private insurance company had changed!  After that I started getting calls from supposedly IRDA, asking  if I have any problems with my insurance! I shared the whole problem, believing them to be from IRDA! I was asked if I was satisfied with the agents service because his commission depends on customer satisfaction! I told them I have never been contacted by any agent or anybody in these 5 years! The calling party said but we have a signed document saying you have signed a satisfaction certificate! When I protested that this must be forged, I was asked to come to an office at the other end of Delhi to verify it! I requested them to meet me at any close by branch as I am a senior citizen! I was also asked if I would like to talk to the agent first.? I agreed. The calling party said they'd call back but never did! The number from which they called also used to go unanswered! I finally managed to retrieve the money I had deposited with a small interest as I was "breaking" the policy term! On close scrutiny I discovered to my horror, the policy they had sold me was for a term of 50 years! I was 58 or so when I took that "policy"! And it was some kind of mutual fund! Never explained at the time this was "sold" to me! 
Lesson: never let any agent say: leave this, just sign here! NEVER EVER TRUST EVEN YOUR RELATIONSHIP MANAGER & BLINDLY SIGN ON ANYTHING! THERE ARE TOO MANY UNSCRUPULOUS BASTARDS ON THE LOSE! 
I wish you luck to be able to retrieve all your money, at least the invested amount. Mine happened before the lockdown. I dread to think what would have happened if it was now!

Greetings!! Ma'am Neetu Bhatia,
I agree with the majority of your points and you have raised reasonable concerns. I am grateful to have such a knowledgeable audience on my channel. In conclusion, I'd like to respectfully suggest that society is built on trust values, and we can't expect everybody to know everything. A doctor should have faith in an engineer, and vice versa. These people put their trust in their bankers and advisors, but they were duped. It's not correct to say that this is totally their fault. I hope you would appreciate my concerns. Yes, I agree that the Thakurs should have been a little more cautious. BUT
These policies would not have been issued at all if the insurance provider had issued them after verifying Thakur family's income sources and understanding their needs and requirements, which all insurance companies are required to check under regulatory guidelines. Also, if the insurance firm had followed the provisions for Pre-Issuance Verification Calls to the letter, this mess might have been avoided. The insurance firm failed to perform as intended, and the family is being punished because their money has been forfeited and will now belong to Icici's coffers.
In the same way that banks check whether a customer has enough money to pay the EMIs on a loan, insurance companies are required (by Law) to check whether a customer has enough money to keep paying premiums or not. Selling insurance only after understanding the needs and requirements of the customer is the duty of the insurer.
Do not forget to subscribe to our channel and watch our most recent video, in which we discuss how we assisted a senior citizen who was defrauded of Rs. 3.5 crore by HDFC Life and RBL Bank employees: https://youtu.be/d2ErOFnuYwE  Keep an eye out for the end of the video, where the client's daughter can be seen applauding our efforts.

comments.text: No, an insurance policy is not compulsory to be taken out in combination with a loan. However, a term life insurance policy or a group life insurance policy should be considered to cover the loan. As a result, the possibility of the loan repayment burden being passed to the family in the event of the loan applicant's untimely death will be reduced. Banking executives, on the other hand, rely on consumers purchasing costly and ineffective insurance plans in order to meet their goals, which is absolutely unconstitutional, unethical, and immoral. We are battling against such insurance sales. Else, I must say that a term and health insurance policy are a must-have in every individual's financial planning.

Greetings! Rahul Rajput, Sir
I'm happy you asked this question because it allows us to explain the fraud in greater detail.
Let me respond by stating that this family was sold multiple insurance policies under the guise of issuing (hybrid) fixed deposits without following the regulating authorities' norms and regulations, and the amount deposited by this family in these multiple insurance policies is now at risk of being forfeited by the insurance company because this family is unable to continue paying premiums. The insurance policy was supposed to check whether or not the client could afford to pay the premiums on these policies on a regular basis, and since insurance company failed to do so, the family is being punished while the insurance company benefits, despite the fact that the insurance company is solely to blame.

I agree to some extent with your views. But I would like to humbly submit that this problem would not have arisen and these policies would not have been issued if at all the company had followed the rules and norms as prescribed by the regulator. If PIVC was correctly and religiously followed or if the client's source of funds would have been properly analysed etc. we would not have been discussing this case today. Also you need to understand that multiple insurance policies have been sold to this family under the garb of issuing (hybrid) fixed deposits without following the norms and regulations of the regulating authorities and now the amount deposited by this family in these multiple insurance policies is under danger of getting forfeited by the insurance company because this family is not in a position to continue premium payment in these policies. The insurance company was required to verify (basis income documents) if or not the client can make regular premium payment in these policies or not, before issuing so many policies and because the insurance company did not performed it's task properly (as is mandated by IRDAI) the family is getting punished and the insurance company is being benefitted (because the forfeited money would go into their coffers) although the major (if not entire) fault is of the insurance company only.

Dear Colin Sir,
I agree to your points to some extent but don't you think if the bank or the underwriting team of the insurance company had followed the prescribed policy issuance guidelines of the regulator, these policies could not have been issued at all. Bcoz the Pre Issuance Verification Call process was not adhered, the customer's source of funds and income sources were not verified prior to issuance of these policies. Is this only the fault of the client and does the insurance and banking company do not hold any responsibility? The bank and the insurance company are also required to follow the principles of fiduciary responsibility towards it's clients and is also required to keep in mind the insurance principles like Principle of utmost Good faith and Principle of insurable interest etc. before issuance of these unwanted and undesired policies. Points to ponder upon...Many regards and thanks for initiating such a worthy and knowledge based discussion

comments.text:
Dear Sir,
To some extent you are right. The cheating was actually started by the sales employee who gave wrong information about the product and in name of hybrid FD he sold insurance policy. But our concern is also about why was the financial underwriting team allowing issuance of so many policies without verification of income documents. As per AML guidelines issued by the regulator policies of all customers with annual premium more than 1 lakh rupees are subject to extra due diligence and the insurance company is mandated to verify the source of funds of the customer and check if the customer would be in a position to continue premium payment for several years or not. If the source of funds are found to be not satisfactory then such policies should not be issued. In these cases no such guideline was followed. Also the practice of Pre Issuance Verification call was not performed by the company religiously. On the top of all these wrong practices now the grievance department of the company is also overlooking all such wrong practices of its own employees and is infact questioning the client. Is this not enough to conclude that somewhere all the departments of the company are involved in this loot and is it possible that such practices are happening without the knowledge and cognizance of the senior management of the company.

Ash
Never mix insurance and investment.
Always keep investment and insurance separate.
Go for pure term insurance for insurance purpose. And do FD or MF or RD  for investment, as per your risk appetite.

Be very rude against any sale pitch, never try to show your good face, try to appear very cunning and never accept any financial product which is offered to you by someone.
Financially educate, and buy financial products by your choice and depending upon your needs, not because someone offered it to you.

If someone want to sale any financial product and you are unable to appear harsh, you just ask time for due diligence and in follow-up call just refuse the product siting any reason.

There are plenty of readymade reasons.
Eg - 
Less liquidity than mutual fund.
Many charges and fee ( Fund allocation charges, fund management charge, policy administration charge, fund switching charge), 
Low return in case of market crash.
Less sum insured in comparison to term policy.

comments.text:
Never mix insurance and investment.
Always keep investment and insurance separate.
Go for pure term insurance for insurance purpose. And do FD or MF or RD  for investment, as per your risk appetite.

Be very rude against any sale pitch, never try to show your good face, try to appear very cunning and never accept any financial product which is offered to you by someone.
Financially educate, and buy financial products by your choice and depending upon your needs, not because someone offered it to you.

If someone want to sale any financial product and you are unable to appear harsh, you just ask time for due diligence and in follow-up call just refuse the product siting any reason.

There are plenty of readymade reasons.
Eg - 
Less liquidity than mutual fund.
Many charges and fee ( Fund allocation charges, fund management charge, policy administration charge, fund switching charge), 
Low return in case of market crash.
Less sum insured in comparison to term policy.

When you receive the documents, you will understand that it is a policy. Thereafter you have 15 days to go through the policy and if you're uncomfortable with it, you can cancel it by going to the nearest insurance company branch. Noteworthy is to check the policy term, premium payment term and date of last premium and maturity date. A small activity will save anyone from such situations. 
People cannot trust anybody blindly. In insurance parlance there are no such terms like interest or RD or FD. You can see single premium, monthly payment of premium, bonus or additions. Best tool against these problems is using the 15 days free look period. RBI takes cognizance of such complaints against banks. IRDAI too takes stringent action.

comments.text:
Simple rule..stay faaaaar way from insurance as an investment .. including all those ulip, pension plans , endowment plans etc..so complex , loaded with fees and restrictions .
Use insurance as a risk mitigation tool alone to insure against loss of future earnings incase some thing unfortunate happens. 
Just have staggered pure term policies of various maturities that will periodically expire one by one as you age and build your savings.

For investments if you have a longer than 5 to 7 year horizon , nothing beats sip in good equity funds .
Esp consumer , consumption , health care and mnc funds for india and sip in us centric  international blue chip  mutual funds that are usually loaded with great us companies like microsoft and Google.

For more tax efficient deployment ,go for sip in  good equity funds with upto 30% international exposure to get benefits of long term capital gains tax rates.

Simple .but few financial advisors will tell you this.

comments.text:
Dear Sir,
Out of the 14 policies sold to this family only 2 are ULIP and rest all the policies are traditional i.e. they have premium forfeiture clause. The premium deposited in all these 12 policies is at risk of forfeiture and therefore your concern of collusion of these clients with the agent is completely baseless. Who would risk the entire premium getting forfeited for a meagre of commission. No sensible human being would do that. Also as per AML guidelines to be mandatorily followed by the insurance company, the insurance companies have been clearly made responsible for verifying client's source of funds and issue insurance policies only after understanding the needs and requirements of the client. Also as per IRDAI's protection of policyholder's interest regulations the insurance companies have been mandated to make Pre Issuance Verification call to their customers explaining them the terms of the policy and are required to keep a call recording. You would be surprised to know that company has till date not provided this call recording for any of the 12 policies issued after 2017. Hope this clarifies all your doubts.

comments.text:
“Buyer Beware “...for anything from anyone,anywhere in the world.
Never buy a product from the same bank you have most of your assets.
If they want to commit automatic fraud they cannot because there is no money in that account and will have to contact you.
always read,re-read every document,Make copies after signing and keep copy of crossed cheques,fully dated.
Do not give post dated cheques.let them clear the documents from authorities before writing cheques .
Do not have safe deposit lockers in same bank.
Have multiple immediate family members sign on the locker form and make copies.
Make proper “Last Will” for each member separately and get it registered.
Keep all original documents in one locker and copies in another locker with full access to beneficiaries.
If you don’t have bank key or documents ,bank manager will not allow you to open after death of person and then theft can happen by bank employees, because they know you don’t have any authority to open and need court order.
During this time good stuff is removed by some bank official because they have keys and know it will take time.
They are owners of bank access.
If branch is closing you must immediately go and remove everything...don’t expect all lockers to be moved.
Bank sends you notice....don’t delay.
Make sure all house documents and property ownership documents are fully accessible to immediate family members along with back up beneficiaries of bank accounts.
No money...no lawyer..no court fees.
Prepare for all events and leave all emotions to the past.
This is reality...zero trust because everyone wants money at all costs.
Penalties are very low and so people take chances.
If you cannot prove that property or finances belong to you or your family,it will be hard.
Again...”Buyer Beware”.....get help from other family members or friends or go online to verify.

comments.text:
When employees are lured with incentives on every policy sold, this is bound to happen. And this happens everywhere, be it banks, stock brokers, insurance companies ... this mis-selling is done just because of a small token of amount called incentive. I think relevant regulators must make it mandatory to pass on the incentive to sellers only upon maturity of the product being sold in the insurance induetry or only after the client makes profit, in case of stock broking. That is when  such mis-selling will be curbed.

Don't forget, it's a rat race that even the executives are a part of.. everyone wants to earn more.. one must note, salaries of executives aren't as high as it may seem. In order to earn a bit more, they are forced to mis-sell.. everyone  wants to climb up the corporate ladder quicker than the other.. till the incentive norms are tightened, such things will keep happening...and there won't be any end to itm. It's high time that the RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and other regulators wake up and do the needful.. 

Again.. the culprit is the entity instigating it's employees to sell the irrelevant products to relevant customers. One of my classmates in PG was fired by one of these banks for telling the truth about these policies to customers..
